question: What is 'eye-trace', one of Murch's considerations when cutting between shots?
answer: Where the viewer's eye is looking on the screen at the moment of a cut. If the next shot puts something important in the same area, the cut feels smooth; if it makes the eye leap across the frame, it can jar. Murch shows how editors steer an audience's gaze from shot to shot.
move: Good cuts lead the eye to where it is already looking.
simply: Watch where your eyes go at a cut. Good editors place the next important thing right where you're already looking.
why: Designers use the same idea in apps and web pages: put the next thing where the eye lands. Noticing it shows you when you're being guided.
